p: Our Father which art in heaven: A form of true prayer.

day by day our daily bread: That is, as much as is needed for us this day, by which we are not prevented from having an honest care for the maintenance of our lives; but that complaining care, which kills a number of men, is cut off and restrained.
And he said unto them: We must pray with faith.

importunity he will rise and give: Literally, "impudence": but that impudency which is spoken of here is not to be found fault with, but is very commendable before God, for he is well pleased by such importunity.
But some of them said: An example of horrible blindness, and such as cannot be healed, when the power of God is blasphemed by an evil conscience and pretended malice.
But he: The true way to know the true Christ from the false is this, that the true Christ has no harmony or agreement with Satan: and once we know him it is left for us to acknowledge him.
through Beelzebub: By the name and power of Beelzebub.
finger of God cast out devils: That is, by the power of God: so it says in Geneva "Ex 8:19".
palace: The word properly signifies an open and empty room in front of a house, and so in translation is taken for noblemen's houses.
He that is not with me: Against indifferent men, and such as love to have a compromise, who seek means to reconcile Christ and Satan together.
When the unclean spirit is gone: He that does not continue, but is in a worse case, than he that never began.
And it came to pass: Christ does not seek praise for himself, but in our salvation.
No man: Our minds are therefore lightened with the knowledge of God, that we should give light unto others, and therefore our main labour ought to be to pray for that light.
And as he spake: The service of God consists not in outward cleanliness and planned rites or ceremonies, but in the spiritual righteousness of the heart and charity.

of such things as ye have: That is, according to your ability: as one would say, instead of your extortion which hindered you so that you could not eat cleanly, use charity, and in accordance with your ability be good to the poor, and in this way will that which is within the platter be sanctified even though the platter is unwashed.
But woe unto you: It is the characteristic of hypocrites to stand firmly for little trifles and to let greater matters pass.
tithe mint and rue and: You decide by God's law that the tenth part is due to be paid.

all manner of herbs: Of all types of herbs, some as Augustine expounds it in his Enchiridion to Laurence, chap. 99, where he shows in like manner how that place of Paul, (God "will have all men to be saved"), 1Ti 2:4, is to be expounded after the same manner.

judgment and the love of God: That is to say, that which is right and reasonable to do, for this word "judgment" contains the commandments of the second table, and the other words, "the love of God", contain the commandments of the first.
Woe unto you: Hypocrisy and ambition are commonly joined together.
Woe unto you: Hypocrites deceive men with an outward show.
Then answered one of the lawyers: Hypocrites are very severe against other men, but think that all things are lawful for themselves.
Woe unto you: Hypocrites honour those saints when they are dead whom they persecute most cruelly when they are alive.

ye bear witness that ye allow: When you persecute God's servants like mad men, even as your fathers did, though you try and cover it with a pretence of godliness, yet nonetheless, by beautifying the sepulchres of the prophets, what else are you doing but glorying in your father's cruelty, and setting up monuments (as it were) in glory and triumph of it?
persecute: They will so vex them and trouble them, that at length they will banish them.
shed from the foundation of the: That you may be called to give an account for it, yea, and be punished for the shedding of that blood of the prophets.
Woe unto you: Those who ought to be the door keepers of the Church have for a long time mainly hindered the people from entering into the knowledge of God.
taken away the key of knowledge: You have hidden and taken away, so that it cannot be found anywhere.
And as he said these things: The more the world is reprehended, the worse it is, and yet we must not betray the truth.
provoke him to speak of many: They proposed many questions to him, to draw something out of his mouth which they might traitorously find fault with.
